text:
marta: Heads-up — getting multiple customer reports of p95/p99 spikes on /v1/generate in eu-west this morning. Started ~07:10 UTC. Errors are low but latency at p99 has doubled vs baseline. Anyone on-call?
omar: I'm on it. Can you paste a sample request (headers + body) and a request id if available?
sophia: Customer ticket 5739 attached — they provided a request id: req_eu_3f9a. They say 200 responses but slow tail.
lee: I see a small bump on infra graphs. Instance CPU ok but GPUs show increased context-switching and higher kernel time. No obvious OOMs.
marta: Relevant deploys? Any canaries overnight in eu-west?
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy rollout v2.3.4 -> eu-west-1 completed at 06:58 UTC (canary 10%). No rollback.
alexa: That canary changed batching and KV-cache behavior (enabled aggressive prefix caching for chat sessions).
omar: Start checklist for latency regression: 1) reproduce with same request id via debug proxy 2) check model variant routing 3) check batching/queue stats 4) fallback/mitigation options.
sophia: Customer repro steps: same prompt repeated 50x with short context; they said p99 ~ 1.1s baseline, now hitting 2.3–3.2s.
marta: Omar, try repro from eu-west via the debug proxy and include X-Redwood-Request-ID in headers.
omar: Reproducing now. curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "X-Redwood-Request-ID: req_eu_3f9a" -d '{"model":"redwood-2","input":"<redacted>","max_tokens":256}' https://eu-west.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
lee: While Omar runs that, I pulled serving runtime metrics: queue depth spikes at ~0.6s before token generation; kernel stalls correlate with longer sequence-length requests. Single-token latencies mostly fine — tail spikes when batch contains a mix of long/short sequences.
alexa: That matches the canary change — aggressive prefix caching plus larger dynamic batches can cause head-of-line blocking when long contexts are batched with short ones.
marta: Mitigation playbook idea (short-term): 1) Enable request-size-aware batching (cost-based grouping) 2) Cap max batch size for real-time routes 3) Open circuit-breaker on the canary pool to route to stable pool 4) Fallback to smaller/quantized model if latency > threshold 5) Apply per-team rate limits to reduce burstiness.
sophia: Can we hit circuit-breaker now for the canary pool and route to stable? Customer is affected.
alexa: I can trigger a manual routing policy flip — move traffic from canary -> stable for /v1/generate in eu-west. Doing it now: policy change requested.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Traffic routing policy update applied: canary pool traffic -> stable-pool (immediate).
lee: After routing flip, monitoring shows p99 dropping within 2 minutes to ~1.2s. Good sign.
omar: Repro after flip: p99 for req_eu_3f9a is back to ~1.15s. Will keep running a few more samples.
marta: Intermediate takeaways: likely combination of batch-mixing + cache behavior change in canary. Root cause candidate: batch scheduling algorithm allowed large batch windows that grouped long sequences with short ones, increasing p99.
alexa: Long-term fixes: 1) Add cost-aware batching at runtime (tokens * model_cost) 2) Implement per-request latency SLO guardrail that triggers circuit-breaker before customer impact (e.g., if p99 exceeds 1.5x baseline for 3m) 3) Expose per-route per-model p95/p99 in console + alerts for regressions 4) Canary rollback-by-default if tail latency regresses beyond threshold.
sophia: For customers impacted, offer priority reroute to stable and SLA credit if regression hits SLA window? We should draft comms.
marta: Operational action items (assign): - omar: collect and attach sample traces + flamegraphs for canary runtime (due in 2 hours) - lee: implement temporary max_batch_size cap for eu-west real-time routing (10ms window / max 8) (due 30m) - alexa: add circuit-breaker rule for canary pools tied to p99 windows (due 1h) - sophia: draft customer-facing note and ticket updates (due 45m)
omar: Started traces collection. Initial flamegraph shows long-tail scheduling stalls in batching thread.
lee: Patching batching config now: set max_batch_tokens=4096, max_batch_items=8, and enable strict cost-grouping: true. Applying to eu-west real-time runtime.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Runtime config patch applied to eu-west real-time at 07:45 UTC.
lee: Rolling metrics show queue wait down and p99 trending to baseline after config patch + routing change.
sophia: Updating ticket 5739: informed customer we routed them to stable infra and are actively investigating root cause + mitigation steps. They replied :thumbsup:.
marta: Postmortem scope: incident window 07:10–07:48 UTC, trigger = canary batching config change, primary impact = p99 regression for /v1/generate in eu-west, mitigations = routing flip + batching cap.
alexa: Proposal for SLO guardrails doc snippet: "SLO guardrail: For any route, if p99 latency > 1.5x baseline for 5 consecutive 1-minute windows, auto-enable circuit-breaker that sends new requests to fallback model/region until p99 returns below 1.2x". Also add cost threshold to avoid over-fallback for low-cost requests.
omar: Also recommend adding a canary safety net: any canary that modifies batching or cache behavior must start with 1% traffic and include an automated tail-latency comparison job. If p95/p99 grows > 20% within first 30 minutes, auto-scale down canary to 0%.
marta: Good. Let's capture these in the playbook. For now, keep the canary disabled and monitor for 2 hours. Postmortem doc later.
sophia: I'll send customer follow-up in 15m. Thanks team. :handshake:
lee: I'll keep real-time dashboard alerts tuned and add a new alert: "batch-mix tail latency" when queue_wait_95 > 400ms and batch_variance_high.
alexa: I'll draft the guardrail rules and config snippets to add to the console (rate limits, circuit-breaker thresholds, fallback model mapping).
marta: Closing here once we have traces + postmortem draft. Great response, folks. :rocket:
